categories.implied-object: A situation implies an unnamed object the speaker or character is using or looking for (cactus-style).
categories.bridge-entity: Two-step factual prompt; the unstated intermediate entity is the concept, not the final answer.
categories.described-entity: A definition or description of a thing, place or person whose name is never given.
categories.implied-cause: A scene shows only consequences; the concept is the unstated cause or event.
categories.implied-emotion: Behaviour or body language implies a character's unnamed emotion or state.
categories.implied-intention: Preparations imply what a character is about to do or secretly plans.
categories.list-category: A list of items whose shared category or common property is never named.
categories.foreign-language: Non-English text implying a word; accepted in English or in the text's own language.
categories.garbled-word: A misspelled, scrambled, truncated or obfuscated word; the concept is the intended word.
categories.riddle-metaphor: Riddles, metaphors and euphemisms that stand for an unstated literal concept.
categories.control: Plain text with no particular hidden concept; shows what a lens prints when there is nothing to find.
